# iliad-029 (5.217–317) — reviewer report

Two passes, both over `units.json`: `drafts/iliad-029/gloss.json` did not exist when the review ran, so the glossary pass (parse of every form against its line) has NOT been done and must be run by whoever reviews the gloss. Pass 2 was a second full read of the units after the edits below. No modern translation was opened. `t` was not touched (checked: all 61 `t` identical before and after). Nothing built, committed or pushed.

Speech marks checked: iliad-028 ends with Pandarus’ speech closed (”) at 5.216, so 5.217 correctly opens in narration with no mark. All nine speeches (218–228, 230–238, 243–250, 252–273, 277–279, 284–285, 287–289) open with “ on the first unit (with `mark`) and close with ” on the last; opens and closes balance in both `l` and `i`. Paragraph flags `p` sit exactly on the ten ¶ lines (217, 229, 239, 251, 274, 280, 286, 290, 297, 311). The mid-line reuse of 5.229, 5.251, 5.259, 5.283 matches the published English; 5.280 and 5.312 follow the published wording for the line concerned. Hand scan of 5.247 (the only flagged line): Αἰ-νεί | ας δ’ υἱ | ὸς μὲν ἀ | μύ-μο-νος | Ἀγ-χί | σα-ο, 14 syllables with a spondee in the fifth foot; the irregularity is real and the note already carried a sentence, which I made say where.

## Findings considered and refused

- 218 (and 252) `l` leaves the particle δ’ untranslated (“Do not speak so” for μὴ δ’ οὕτως). Refused: a bare connective at the opening of a speech does not translate cleanly, `i` and the note carry the sense; the note on 218 says “and not”, and I added the δ’ comment at 252.
- 219 “chariot” singular against the table’s 4.297 “chariots”. Refused as an error (the context is one car); recorded as a declared departure instead (change 21).
- 247 `n` “ἀμύμων … what the word means is not known” and 218-onward uses of “plural for one vehicle”. Left: consistent with the house table.
- 233 `n` “μή … takes both the future ματήσετον and the subjunctives”. Considered a possible error (a future after μή); refused, μή with the future indicative is attested after verbs of fearing and the note’s claim is accurate.
- 277 `n` gives δαΐφρων as ‘wise-hearted’ while `l` has “wise-minded”. Refused: this is the table’s own `l`/`i` pair (4.252 row), and the note states the doubt.
- 239–240 `i` “drove” for ἔχον (`l` “held”). Refused: ‘held (on a course)’ is what the note calls a stock phrase for driving a team on, and the table has no row against it.
- 261–264 `i` “made fast” for τείνας (`l` “stretched”). Refused: it is a stated interpretation in the note and in new-renderings, consistent with ἄντυξ.
- 248 `l` “claims to be born” for the perfect infinitive ἐκγεγάμεν. Refused: idiomatic enough, matches `i`.
- 281 `l` “was brought near to the breastplate” (πελάσθη) vs `i` “came up against”. Refused: sense agrees.
- Remembered-English check: no phrase in `i` read as an imported translation line; nothing changed on that ground.


## Pass 2 — gloss.json (179 novel entries, 20 `__broaden__` entries)

Every novel parse was read against its line(s) in the reviewed units; all 179 novel forms are present, none extra; all entries under 230 characters, typographic ’ only, no "here", no line numbers. All 20 `__broaden__` values begin with the existing entry from `iliad-glossary.json` whole, then " · " and the new reading, and each new reading is true of a form in this part (αὐτῶν 256, γενέθλη 270, δείσας 298, κτείνῃ 236, λίθος 308, μέγ’ 285, μένος 254/296, μή 233, νῶϊ 224/235, οἵ 248, τεὸν 234, ἀγόρευε 218, ἐθέλητον 233, ἑὸν 314, ἔλαυνε 237, ἔχ’ 230, ὀρέξῃ 225/260, ὑπ’ 267, τις 316).

### Changes

| ματήσετον | novel entry; units 233 `n` | major | Parse "fut. 3 dual (or short-vowel subj.)" left the question open and did not match the unit note, which called it a future. The form is ambiguous (fut. indic. and short-vowel aor. subj. coincide); the clause is built on subjunctives (ἐθέλητον, κτείνῃ, ἐλάσσῃ) after μή, so the subjunctive is the parse that fits. | Entry now "aor. subj. 3 dual, short-vowel, after μή (the form could also be fut. 3 dual)", lemma ματάω as in the note; unit 233 note rewritten to match (no longer says "takes the future ματήσετον"). The μή broaden ("’lest’ with a dual verb in -ετον") already fits and was kept. |

The genitive is the relative attracted into the case of its antecedent τῆς γενεῆς; the exchange idea is carried by ποινήν. | "relative, fem. gen. sg., attracted into the case of its antecedent: ’which’ (τῆς … γενεῆς ἧς ’the breed which’)"; old entry kept whole. |

Pass 2 counts: major 2, minor 14 (16 entries). The broaden list now has 28 entries (20 original, 8 added).

### Considered and refused (gloss)

- δέδεξο "perf. imper." (vs reduplicated aorist): the form is genuinely classed both ways and neither is demonstrably wrong; the unit note says only "reduplicated imperative". Left.
- ἄνδρε "masc. nom. dual": correct for its only occurrence (303); the 244 form is ἄνδρ’, handled by the new ἄνδρ broaden.
- κτείνῃ "pres. subj." (old entry kept): κτείνῃ is identical in present and aorist; not wrong.
- ὅς: the indefinite use in ὅς τις (301) is covered by the τις broaden; no ὅς broaden added.
- σιγαλόεντα "gleaming" in the gloss: house word-choice applies to `l`/`i`, and the entry marks the sense uncertain. Left.
- εἰωθότι "used to the horses": slightly specific but the parse is true and not pinned to a line number. Left.
- οἷοι, πώς, ἐθέλητον readings: checked against 222, 304, 250/298, 233; correct.
